note: Occasions are ordinary application state, authored by a person through a form — the same way you would put an event in a calendar. No model creates one, reads one, or infers one. `avoid` is constrained to the allergen vocabulary the recipes declare against, so an occasion cannot reference an allergen no dish knows about. This is the FAST pace layer: it exists for a fortnight and then it expires. `scheduledOn` is when the person filled the form: before that date the occasion does not exist, which is why the household's ordinary page is the one you get until they plan something.
dates: DELIBERATELY IN THE PAST, and do not move them forward. While an occasion is live the learner's page is an occasion page — it leads with ComparisonTable at hero and carries a shopping list — because TechniqueThread requires `state.hasOccasion == false`. That silently costs the demo its best beat: a recipe site with no recipe on it. These dates sit inside the ninety-day log window, so the dinner reads as something that happened and expired, which is the pace-layer argument anyway. Every moment of the occasion beat is still reachable with `?today=`, and /start derives its links from these two fields rather than from a table of dates, so moving them moves the links with them. A future date would only postpone the problem: real time would arrive at it.
